title: Appeal of RE Moon K. Ham v. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: Ham’s appeal was sustained, and the Presbytery’s and its Judicial Commission’s actions adjudicating and censuring him were reversed. No remand was ordered.
first_summary: A ruling elder appealed his three-year suspension from the sacraments, challenging Korean Capital Presbytery’s authority to adjudicate charges against him. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery’s and its Judicial Commission’s actions because original jurisdiction over a communicant member belonged to the member’s Session. The decision invalidated the censure on jurisdictional grounds without ordering a remand.
summary: A ruling elder appealed Korean Capital Presbytery’s three-year suspension of him from the sacraments. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery’s and its Judicial Commission’s actions because original jurisdiction over a communicant member belonged to his local Session. The ruling rests on the identity of the proper court, not the merits of the charges, and orders no remand or further relief.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The actions were reversed because Session, not Presbytery or its commission, had original jurisdiction over a communicant member. Printed pp. 128–129; lines 60–76.
